subject: Per-token ladder request + implementation constraints
messages:
From: John Doyle <john.doyle@acmehealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: hosted API per-token ladder (commits + true-up)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the call today. Procurement asked me to follow up with a few concrete asks so we can start informal pricing:

- We plan to commit to a year-long consumption profile (monthly forecast attached).
- Want a clear ladder with breakpoints for per-token pricing (monthly commit tiers).
- Need to understand: do you price on a marginal basis (each token at the breakpoint rate) or blended (single effective rate for total usage)?
- For budgeting we want a sample invoice projection with 1) conservative ramp, 2) stretch ramp, and 3) a mechanism for under/over usage true-ups.

Could you send an example construct and any standard contract language you recommend for true-ups and fallback rates? Attached is our initial commit profile (acme_commit_profile.xlsx).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement hopes to lock terms before their next board meeting on August 10.

Thanks,
John Doyle
Procurement Manager
Acme Health

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: John Doyle <john.doyle@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: hosted API per-token ladder (commits + true-up)

Hi John — thanks for the profile and the clear asks. I attached a Redwood ladder template (redwood_ladder_template.xlsx) and sketched two common constructions below so you can see the practical differences.

Quick summary:
- Marginal ladder: each breakpoint applies only to incremental tokens in that band. Preferred when you want explicit incentives for incremental growth and tight unit economics visibility.
- Blended (effective) rate: a single average per-token price computed across all usage. Simpler for invoicing but less aligned to marginal cost; better for customers who want a predictable single line item.

Example constructs (high level):
1) Committed monthly tiers (marginal):
   - 0-50M tokens: $0.0035/token
   - 50M-200M tokens: $0.0028/token
   - 200M+ tokens: $0.0022/token
   - Invoice = sum(tokens_in_band * band_rate) + overage rules for bursts above committed monthly cap.

2) Committed annual blended (effective):
   - Commit: 24B tokens/year -> effective rate $0.0029/token applied to total monthly consumption; true-up annually against committed buckets.

Questions that change the model:
- Do you need monthly true-ups or quarterly/annual? Monthly true-ups are operationally heavier but keep billing aligned.
- Do you want a hard monthly cap with overage pricing or a soft cap with throttled burst tolerance?

Next steps I recommend:
1) Tell us preferred true-up cadence (monthly/quarterly/annual).
2) Confirm whether you prefer marginal incentives or a single blended rate for billing simplicity.

I'll draft a short example invoice projection for your conservative and stretch ramp once we have those two answers. Looping Ben to scope engineering/throughput considerations if you need burst tolerance in contract language. Laura, can you flag any finance constraints for Acme-style commitments?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: hosted API per-token ladder (internal margin math)

Laura / Olga — forwarding John's request and my quick margin sketch. For Acme's profile in the attached workbook, marginal vs blended makes a material difference to our revenue recognition and GPU allocation planning. Key points:

- If they want monthly hard caps + instantaneous overage, we need an SLA for sustained bursts; that impacts Dedicated capacity allocation and spike credit calculations.
- Suggested breakpoint set (internal): 75M / 250M / 1B monthly. These smooth the cliff and keep margin >= 30% at 250M.
- Clawback / true-up language proposal (internal draft): quarterly true-ups with a 10% tolerance band before credits apply; annual reconciliation for billing true-up to preserve revenue predictability.

I'll prepare two sample invoices in the template: conservative ramp (50% of forecast month1, +20% month-on-month) and stretch ramp (forecast *1.4). Olga — if Acme wants blended, the effective rate for the conservative scenario lands ~ $0.00295/token; marginal scenario yields variable line items but average ~ $0.0027/token for Year1 in my sketch.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: John Doyle <john.doyle@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: hosted API per-token ladder (commits + true-up)

John — thanks, and apologies for the slower follow-up. We reviewed internally and sketched both invoice projections (conservative / stretch) in the attached template. High-level recommendation:

- If Acme prioritizes cost predictability for internal budgeting -> go with an annual blended effective rate with quarterly true-ups. We can give a 1% discount vs monthly-blended if you commit to annual reconciliation.
- If Acme prioritizes aligned growth incentives -> go with a marginal ladder with breakpoints (we recommend 75M / 250M / 1B monthly) and quarterly true-ups with a 10% tolerance band.

Operational ask: specify whether you prefer hard monthly caps or soft caps with overage billing. For hard caps we'll include explicit overage rates and a burst policy (sustained bursts > 10 minutes will be subject to throttling unless you buy burst credits).

Attached: redwood_ladder_template.xlsx (with our two invoice scenarios) and a clean snippet of contract language for true-ups and overages. If that all looks good I can route a short SOW + order form for signature (we can do DocuSign and propose a 30-day trial of Dedicated burst credits during ramp).

If you want, we can jump on a 30-minute call next week to walk the numbers with Laura from finance and Ben on the technical guardrails.

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
